summary: Ibrahim Shah is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Muhammad Farooq Swati. He served as Associate Professor and Department Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959), where he later held a post attested from 1977 to 1993, and taught at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies and archaeology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita, he taught at Nishogakusha, Kokugakuin, Tohoku (~1952–1965), Seijo, and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani Universities under Kogen Mizuno. He taught at Komazawa University from 1975, serving as professor from 1985 to 2013.

Ichiro Numata works in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2026, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and history. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome, where he subsequently served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940). He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and Pravda.

Ihsan Ali is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin, he has served as Professor at Peshawar, Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009), and Director of Archaeology and Museums.

Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Komazawa University, having studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

Ikuko Tazaki works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, she was attested as a special researcher at Otani University and an affiliated researcher at Kyoto University's Center for Southeast Asian Studies.

Ikuro Hattori is a scholar of Indology and philosophy holding a PhD from Pune University. He held researcher posts at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2003) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026), also lecturing at Aichi Gakuin University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Juha Pentikäinen, René Gothóni, and Simo Knuuttila. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki from 1984 and visited Oxford.

Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was a philosopher who studied at the Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He later held the chair of logic and metaphysics at Königsberg from 1770.
Imran Philip is an Indology and history researcher who studied for a doctorate under Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Imre Bangha is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University. He has served as Associate Professor of Hindi at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College since ~2003, and at ELTE.

Imre Galambos is a scholar of Sinology and history who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley. He worked at the British Library, served as Professor at Cambridge (2012–2023), and held chairs at Hamburg and Zhejiang University in ~2021.

Imre Hamar is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006.

In-gun Kang is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, Jesuit School of Theology, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes (attested 2012).

Ines Konczak is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.
